prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. Injury: neck and back strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1295; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather keep my name out of the record for now, if that's acceptable. I can give you the basics about the accident.

Q: That's fine for today. Tell me what you remember about the collision in Pearland.

A: I was driving home on a weekday afternoon, in the right lane of a two-lane road with a light traffic flow. A car coming the other way drifted into my lane. I braked and turned slightly, but we still made contact. It was a head-on hit, though not a hard one. My car's airbags did not deploy.

Q: How fast were you traveling at the time?

A: Not fast. Somewhere around the posted limit, maybe a little under. I remember the other car was also moving slowly.

Q: Did you feel anything immediately after the impact?

A: My head snapped forward and then back. My neck felt stiff within a few minutes, and by the next morning my lower back was sore too.

Q: Did you seek medical care?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that evening, and then I followed up with my primary doctor. They diagnosed a neck strain and a lower back strain and gave me a treatment plan.

Q: What did that plan involve?

A: Some physical therapy sessions, a couple of weeks of muscle relaxants, and advice to avoid heavy lifting. I also used a heating pad a lot.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily routine?

A: Mostly in small ways. Driving for longer than about thirty minutes bothers my neck. I had to ask a coworker to cover a few tasks that required bending or lifting. I still go to the gym, but I do fewer exercises and I stop when my back starts to ache.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment?

A: Yes, I still go to physical therapy about twice a week. My doctor says I'm improving, though it's slower than I'd like.

Q: Have you had any prior neck or back complaints?

A: Nothing serious. I had a stiff neck once or twice from sleeping wrong, but I never saw a doctor for it and I never missed work because of my back before this.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you want to add to your answers?

A: Only that I want to be accurate. Some days are better than others, and I'm trying to describe things as they actually are.
